one_liner: Field report: moving Alibaba's Hologres code base from #include headers to C++20 named modules cut its compile time 42%.
what_it_does: This is a technique entry, not a library: replace textual #include of project and standard-library headers with C++20 named modules (export module / import), so each interface is parsed once into a Built Module Interface (BMI) and imported by every translation unit that needs it. Alibaba Cloud reports doing this on the Hologres data-warehouse mainline with its in-house Clang/LLVM-based Alibaba Cloud Compiler, which also ships a modularised standard library (std module). It is not a drop-in switch: sources, the build graph and often the library ABI change, and the build system must scan sources for module dependencies.
how_it_is_fast: Header inclusion re-preprocesses and re-parses the same headers in every translation unit (the post's hello-world example says <iostream> alone expands to about 30,000 lines, roughly 1 MB, under libstdc++); a module interface is compiled once to a BMI and later imports deserialize it lazily. Clang's documentation describes modules as 'a kind of cache to speed up compilation'; Reduced BMIs (-fmodules-reduced-bmi) and, from Clang 19, non-cascading BMI changes cut the rebuilds caused by edits to transitive dependencies. Clang can also preload a prebuilt std BMI with -fmodule-file=<std BMI> to get most of the std-module benefit without rewriting includes.
when_to_use: Large C++ code bases where front-end time on heavy, widely included headers (standard library, template-heavy internal libraries) dominates full builds.
Teams that control the whole toolchain: Clang 16+ (or GCC 14+, MSVC 14.34+) with CMake 3.28+ and Ninja 1.11+, and Clang 18.1.2+ / GCC 15+ / MSVC 14.36+ if you want import std through CMake.
New code or internal libraries that can adopt module interfaces from the start, or libraries that can ship a named-module wrapper next to their headers (the export-using style that keeps the ABI).
Projects whose header hygiene is already good, since duplicated global-module-fragment includes erase much of the gain.
when_not_to_use: Code bases that already build fast with precompiled headers, unity builds or a lightweight core API: the {fmt} author reported no measurable build speed-up from modules over the lightweight core API (search snippet), and the Hologres post's baseline may not have included PCH.

When many module units include the same big headers in their global module fragments: Clang's performance tips warn that duplicated declarations make importers compile more slowly, and an LLVM Discourse thread ('Modules increased build times', snippet only) found half the compile time spent reading modules.

Mixed toolchains or IDE/tooling pipelines that do not yet understand modules, Make-based builds, or Visual Studio generators if you need import std (CMake supports import std only with Ninja generators).
Builds that rely on CMake UNITY_BUILD: scanned module sources are excluded from unity builds.
Shipping libraries to outside users whose ABI must not change: the ABI-breaking transition style changes name mangling and module initializers.

integration.form: language feature (C++20 named modules); no package to install
integration.dependencies: A module-aware compiler and a dependency-scanning build system: CMake 3.28+ with the Ninja (1.11+) or Visual Studio 17 2022+ generators, or xmake; Hologres itself used Alibaba Cloud Compiler (in-house, based on open-source Clang/LLVM, per post snippets).
integration.min_toolchain: C++20. CMake scanning: Clang 16.0+, GCC 14+, MSVC toolset 14.34+ (VS 17.4+). CMake import std: Clang 18.1.2+ with libc++ or libstdc++, GCC 15+ (16+ on macOS), MSVC 14.36+ (VS 17.6+). Hologres compiler version not documented.
integration.platforms: Any platform the compiler supports; the Hologres post's experiments ran on Alibaba Cloud Linux (Alinux, per snippet). CMake notes Ubuntu releases before 26.04 ship broken libstdc++.modules.json files for import std.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the std module can be preloaded with Clang's -fmodule-file without source changes, but converting project headers means writing module interface units, reordering includes and imports, and possibly changing the library ABI.

gotchas: Clang rejects a BMI used with different language-dialect options (for example built with -std=c++20, imported with -std=c++23); every importer must match the module's dialect flags.
#include of a header after an import of a module that already contains it is rejected in Clang today (llvm-project issue #61465); keep includes before imports or move everything to imports.
Clang's cross-TU ODR checking has many false positives and is disabled for the global module fragment by default; BMIs drop the preferred_name attribute, so debuggers show uglier type names.
The reported 0.03 s 'import std' hello-world time excludes building the std module itself, which is precompiled once; the 42% figure does not say whether it covers full or incremental builds.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The siblings (asp staged parsers, RapidProto, Zserio, FlatBuffers, vtprotobuf) speed up generated code at run time; this entry is the one to read when the problem is your own C++ build time rather than parse or serialization speed.
verified_claims_summary: Alibaba Cloud's blog (English and Chinese versions, both seen only through search snippets because the pages did not resolve here) says C++20 modules have run on the Hologres mainline for more than a year and a half and reduced its compile time by 42%, using Alibaba Cloud Compiler built from open-source Clang/LLVM; the baseline is header inclusion with no stated use of precompiled headers, and no compiler version, flags, hardware, build type or full-versus-incremental split is published. Other projects report anything from roughly halving full builds (Infinity, per snippet) to slower builds (LLVM Discourse thread), so the 42% is project-specific.
status_note: Reference-only first-party case study from a closed commercial code base with no public code; the technique itself is standard C++20, and Alibaba's open-source async_simple carries an experimental named-module wrapper (Clang 16+, CMake 3.26+ or xmake) that shows a related, copyable style.
